champion: Meperidine-Induced Skin and Soft Tissue Injury
ordered_diagnoses: Meperidine-Induced Skin and Soft Tissue Injury

facts.raw_span: 7-year history of severe, mechanical, low back pain
long-standing mental depression
self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, 100 mg 4 times per day, for the past 3 years
Large and deep, irregularly shaped, cutaneous ulcer on the dorsum of right forearm with necrotic tissue and muscle exposure at the base
Woody induration of skin on both forearms and abdominal region
Bilateral contracture of deltoid, triceps, and biceps muscles
Active and passive range of motion restricted at shoulders and elbows
No signs of joint inflammation
Elevated serum creatinine kinase (192 U/L; reference range, 0-174 U/L)
Normal complete blood cell count
Shows lobular panniculitis, subcutaneous fat lobules with necrotic adipocytes and dense inflammatory infiltrates composed mainly of foamy histiocytes
Deltoid muscle biopsy showed no muscle involvement

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of large and deep cutaneous ulcers, woody induration of skin, and bilateral contracture of muscles, along with the histopathology results showing lobular panniculitis and dense inflammatory infiltrates, are consistent with scleroderma.

The patient's symptoms of large and deep cutaneous ulcers with necrotic tissue and muscle exposure, along with the histopathology results showing necrotic adipocytes and dense inflammatory infiltrates, are consistent with necrotizing fasciitis.

concepts.preferred_label: Meperidine-Induced Skin and Soft Tissue Injury
concepts.why: The patient's history of self-administering subcutaneous injections of meperidine, along with the symptoms of large and deep cutaneous ulcers and woody induration of skin, are consistent with meperidine-induced skin and soft tissue injury.
The patient's symptoms of bilateral contracture of muscles and restricted range of motion are consistent with contracture.
The histopathology results showing lobular panniculitis and dense inflammatory infiltrates are consistent with panniculitis.
The patient's symptoms of bilateral contracture of muscles and the muscle biopsy results showing no muscle involvement, but with fibrosis, are consistent with muscle fibrosis.
The patient's symptoms of woody induration of skin and the histopathology results showing severe fibrosis in deep dermis and subcutaneous septa are consistent with skin fibrosis.
The patient's symptoms of bilateral contracture of muscles and the histopathology results showing dense inflammatory infiltrates and fibrosis are consistent with myofibrosis.
The patient's symptoms of large and deep cutaneous ulcers with necrotic tissue and the histopathology results showing necrotic adipocytes are consistent with subcutaneous fat necrosis.
The patient's symptoms of elevated serum creatinine kinase and the histopathology results showing dense inflammatory infiltrates are consistent with inflammatory myopathy.

rationales.F03: Meperidine use is a known risk factor for skin and soft tissue injury.
rationales.F04: The presence of a large, deep cutaneous ulcer is highly suggestive of meperidine-induced skin and soft tissue injury and subcutaneous fat necrosis.
rationales.F05: Woody induration of the skin is a characteristic feature of skin fibrosis.
rationales.F06: Bilateral contracture of muscles is a common complication of meperidine-induced skin and soft tissue injury and contracture.
rationales.F07: Restricted range of motion is a common symptom of contracture and muscle fibrosis.
rationales.F08: The absence of joint inflammation makes conditions like inflammatory myopathy less likely.
rationales.F09: Elevated serum creatinine kinase is a marker of muscle damage, which can be seen in muscle fibrosis and myofibrosis.
rationales.F11: The presence of lobular panniculitis and subcutaneous fat necrosis is highly suggestive of meperidine-induced skin and soft tissue injury and panniculitis.
rationales.F12: The absence of muscle involvement on biopsy rules out conditions like inflammatory myopathy and muscle fibrosis.
